cards.text: David, Israel's king, calls in all his leaders, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds. Then he speaks to the whole assembly of Israel, and he's got a BIG plan. But first he checks with them: only if it seems good to them, and only if it's of the LORD their God.

cards.question: Before his plan starts, David wants to send word far and wide. Who does he want to come join them?

answers.text: All their brothers plus the priests and Levites
The kings of the nearby nations

cards.question: David's big plan: all of Israel together will bring back the ___ of God.

cards.text: Every brother in the land, plus the priests, plus the Levites. Friend, that's not a group chat. That's EVERY group chat, all at once, and nobody's allowed to mute it.

cards.question: David looks back to the days of Saul, the king before him. Why does he say they should bring the ark back?

answers.text: They did not inquire of Him in Saul's days
The Philistines are planning to capture it
The priests have begged him to bring it

cards.question: When David shares his plan, half the assembly turns it down.

cards.text: Nope. It seems right to all the people, so the whole assembly agrees, and David gathers all Israel, from the River Shihor in Egypt all the way to Lebo-hamath.
And I thought the junk drawer was crowded. They all go up to Baalah of Judah, also called Kiriath-jearim, to bring up the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim.

cards.question: They bring the ark of God out of the house of Abinadab. What do they carry it on?

cards.text: A NEW cart, with two men, Uzzah and Ahio, guiding it. I bet that thing still has the price sticker on the wheel.

cards.question: As the cart rolls along with the ark, it's a quiet and solemn march for David and the Israelites.

cards.text: Quiet? Songs, harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals AND trumpets, all celebrating before God with all their might! I tried a tambourine in my bakery once, friend. Hopped, missed, and landed face-first in the chocolate chips.
Then the whole parade reaches the threshing floor of Chidon. And the oxen stumble.

cards.question: The oxen pulling the cart stumble at the threshing floor of Chidon. What does Uzzah do?

answers.text: He takes hold of the ark
He jumps down to calm the oxen
He shouts for everyone to stop

cards.text: Then the anger of the LORD burns against Uzzah, and He strikes him down. Uzzah dies right there before God.

cards.question: The text gives the reason: the LORD struck Uzzah down because he had put his ___ on the ark.
When the LORD bursts forth against Uzzah, David becomes angry.

cards.text: David names that place Perez-uzzah, and it's still called that to this day. And that same day, David fears God.

cards.question: That day at Perez-uzzah, David fears God. What does David ask?

answers.text: How can I ever bring the ark of God to me
Who will guide the cart from here on
Where should we go to bury Uzzah

cards.question: After that day, David still takes the ark home with him to the City of David.

cards.text: Instead, David takes it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. Picture opening your front door, and it's the KING: "Hey, can you hold onto this for a while?"

cards.question: The ark of God stays with the family of Obed-edom in his house for three ___.
While the ark of God stays at his house, what happens to Obed-edom's household?

answers.text: The LORD blesses it and all he owns
His family grows afraid and leaves
Sickness spreads all through his house

cards.text: And that's where we'll set the timer down for now, friend. The ark isn't where David planned it to be, and trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "Hey, can you hold onto this for a while?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card goes back to 1 Chronicles 13:2 after card 3 has already moved on to verse 13:3. It only restates the list of invited people from card 2's answer and adds a joke. It adds nothing new and doesn't move the passage forward. Cut it, or move the joke onto a card that carries a new beat.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Abinadab appears here for the first time with no word about who he is. The card names his house and nothing else. A short, sourced description is allowed, for example the man in Kiriath-jearim whose house the ark had been kept in (1 Sam 7:1).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The tambourine joke doesn't land cleanly. "Hopped, missed" doesn't say what he hopped at or missed, so a stranger would say "huh?" It also doesn't share the core action of the verse, which is celebrating before God with all their might. A failed tambourine stunt is about clumsiness, not wholehearted celebration.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "After that day" adds a time the text doesn't give. Verse 13:13 only says David did not move the ark with him to the City of David. The added phrase also makes the statement shaky as a false answer, because in this same story group David later does bring the ark to the City of David (1 Chr 15). A baker who reads "after that day" as "eventually" could argue it's true. Tie the statement to the moment the text describes instead, for example: "David goes ahead and takes the ark with him to the City of David."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The closing line that says the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example. The doc has "And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done." The card has "And that's where we'll set the timer down for now, friend... trust me, this story is NOT done." It needs a line of its own.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
